title: Scientists Filmed Squirrels Hunting and Eating Other Rodents

scenes.text: In 2024, squirrels in California started hunting.
Ground squirrels are the ones with cheeks stuffed full of seeds. One team had watched the same colony for twelve years and never seen a kill.
Then the team came back with video. Squirrels chasing voles, small mouse-like rodents. Catching them. Eating them.
It wasn't one odd animal. Out of 74 encounters with voles that June and July, 42 percent were active hunts. Males, females, even the young.
The trigger was a vole boom. The park was suddenly full of them, and the squirrels simply changed the menu.
The lead scientist's word for it was shocking. After that first video, they saw it almost every day.

description:
In the summer of 2024, California ground squirrels were filmed hunting, killing and eating voles.
It happened at Briones Regional Park in Contra Costa County, in the twelfth year of a long-term study of the colony. Of 74 observed interactions with voles between June and July, 42 percent involved active hunting, by squirrels of all ages and both sexes, during a boom in vole numbers. The study, led by Jennifer E. Smith of the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire with Sonja Wild of UC Davis, appeared in the Journal of Ethology in December 2024.
Would you look at a squirrel the same way again?
subject: ground squirrel
first_comment: One of the scientists said she could barely believe her eyes. What's the most unexpected thing you've seen an animal eat?
